stem.text: A reversible chemical reaction is studied.
The forward reaction has an activation energy Ea = 50 kJ mol–1 and an enthalpy change of reaction ΔHr = +20 kJ mol–1.
When a catalyst is added, the activation energy of the forward reaction decreases by 50%.
What is the activation energy of the backwards reaction when the catalyst is present?

explanation.text: On a reaction pathway diagram, the backward activation energy is the height of the energy barrier above the products. For an endothermic reaction the products sit ΔH above the reactants, so E<sub>a</sub>(backward) = E<sub>a</sub>(forward) − ΔH. A catalyst lowers the peak but does not move the reactant or product levels, so ΔH stays at +20 kJ mol<sup>–1</sup>.

Without the catalyst E<sub>a</sub>(backward) = 50 − 20 = 30 kJ mol<sup>–1</sup>. The catalyst lowers the peak by 25 kJ mol<sup>–1</sup>, which lowers both activation energies by the same amount: 30 − 25 = 5 kJ mol<sup>–1</sup>. The backward barrier falls by the same 25 kJ mol<sup>–1</sup>, not by 50%.

optionAnalysis.text: Adds ΔH to the catalysed forward activation energy (25 + 20) instead of subtracting it; that would be correct only for an exothermic reaction.
This is the catalysed forward activation energy, not the backward one.
Halves the uncatalysed backward activation energy (30 ÷ 2); the catalyst lowers both barriers by the same 25 kJ mol<sup>–1</sup>, not by the same percentage.
Correct. Catalysed forward E<sub>a</sub> = 25 kJ mol<sup>–1</sup>; backward E<sub>a</sub> = 25 − 20 = 5 kJ mol<sup>–1</sup>.

reasoningChain: ΔH is unchanged by the catalyst: +20 kJ mol<sup>–1</sup>, so the products are 20 kJ mol<sup>–1</sup> above the reactants.
Backward E<sub>a</sub> = forward E<sub>a</sub> − ΔH = 25 − 20 = 5 kJ mol<sup>–1</sup>.

inferredMistakes.text: Applying the 50% decrease to the backward activation energy as well (30 → 15).
Adding ΔH instead of subtracting it, which treats the reaction as exothermic.

issues.note: ER 第一条写 'Option D was a common incorrect answer.'，但同一段最后又写 'The correct option is D.'，MS 答案也是 D。两句互相矛盾，第一条里的 D 疑似官方笔误（可能本来是别的字母）。已对照 ER 页面图确认原文如此，逐字照抄未改，请审核。

换行、用 '•' 字符表示子项目，文字没有改。

bullets: Option D was a common incorrect answer.

The forward reaction has an activation energy of 50 kJ mol–1. When this activation energy is halved, by the addition of a catalyst, the activation energy of the forward reaction decreases by 50 percent. The activation energy of the forward reaction therefore becomes 25 kJ mol–1.

When the catalyst is present:
• The activation energy of the forward reaction is 25 kJ mol–1
• The enthalpy change of the forward reaction is +20 kJ mol–1
• The activation energy of the backward reaction is 5 kJ mol–1.

The correct option is D.
